mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against a zero mean return.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month signals strong labor market demand, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in months where PAYEMS exceeds 200.0, with a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates broad-based demand strength, which signals improving corporate revenue outlook and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC drops below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 98.0 (index 2017=100) signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profitability expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below 98.0, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the core CPI inflation rate above 2.5% per annum, combined with a stable federal funds rate, signals persistent inflationary pressure that triggers a forward-looking risk premium increase, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods where CPIAUCSL > 2.5 and FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5, with a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below 400,000 million dollars, coinciding with a decline in GDP growth, signals a weakening demand environment that reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS < 400000.0 and GDPC1 growth < 1.0%, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate above 7.5% and a decline in non-farm payrolls below 135,000 thousand signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer confidence and spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE > 7.5 and PAYEMS < 135000.0, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 98.0, combined with a rising unemployment rate above 7.5%, indicates a dual stress of weak manufacturing output and labor market weakness, which signals a looming recession and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 98.0 and UNRATE > 7.5, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.
